audit.why: EVEN / 6/10 on 52.99% over 368 games. The packet flags the chart as contradicting the win rate (Ornn takes 5 of 7 stages), but that is the actual shape of this lane: Quinn wins the first two levels and then converts the lead off the map with Behind Enemy Lines rather than by continuing to win the lane. The content layer already explains exactly that.
audit.corrected: Rating, diff and tone left alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: Row 4 (Level 6) reads Quinn in both layers; the packet and the audited mirror read Ornn.
audit.why: whys[4] on this very page says 'he owns the direct lane' at 6 and that your R becomes a roam tool rather than a duel button — the row contradicted its own explanation. Call of the Forge God is a 140/120/100s double knockup that flips any all-in.
audit.corrected: Row 4 flipped to Ornn as a matched pair across both layers, with the rating moved from 7/10 to 3/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer calls Volcanic Rupture the 'wall-knockup setup' and treats it as the thing that knocks you up. It is not: Volcanic Rupture is the fissure that plants a magma pillar, and Searing Charge is the knockup — and only when he collides with terrain. The knockup-cancels-your-channel interaction is absent entirely.
audit.why: Riot text — Volcanic Rupture (Q, 9/8.5/8/7.5/7s, 800 range): 'sending out a fissure dealing damage and slowing... a magma pillar forms at the end location'. Searing Charge (E, 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s, 450 range): 'If Ornn collides with terrain while charging, the impact creates a shockwave... knocks up enemies'. Call of the Forge God (R, 140/120/100s) knocks up on the elemental's path and again on his recast charge. Behind Enemy Lines is a channel any CC cancels — both knockups qualify. Bellows Breath's final gout applies Brittle.
audit.corrected: Q re-described as the pillar planter, Searing Charge named as the knockup and stated as terrain-conditional (so open ground beats it), Bellows Breath named as the Brittle source, and the knockup-cancels-your-channel warning added.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere said that Searing Charge needs terrain to knock up.
audit.why: This is the single actionable positioning rule of the lane: stand in the open lane body rather than against the side walls or a fresh pillar and his one kill threat does nothing but damage.
audit.corrected: Written into tldr, dontsFull[0].d and report[5].t.

notes: FLAG MISFIRE, not written to the page: the kit tags Volcanic Rupture with grounding: 'shuts off enemy dashes'. Riot's text for it is damage, slow and a magma pillar — no grounding clause. If Ornn genuinely grounds, Vault denial would belong in dontsFull, so it is worth confirming. Same treatment for the hardCC tag on Bellows Breath: the text only says enemies 'become Brittle', so I attributed the channel cancel to the two explicit knockups (Searing Charge, Call of the Forge God) rather than to W, which is what _missing/quinn.json had suggested. PACKET DEFECT ACKNOWLEDGED: the packet flags the chart as contradicting a 52.99% win rate.
